title: DNS Resolution Recovery
summary: Temporary DNS switch that is offered by the network checker when domain resolution fails. It changes DNS only for the current session and is not a replacement for the permanent DNS Manager.

items.title: Cloudflare DNS (1.1.1.1)
items.description: Writes 1.1.1.1 into /etc/resolv.conf and adds it as a temporary WAN DNS server.
items.usage_tip: Default choice. The original resolv.conf is backed up before the change.

items.title: Google DNS (8.8.8.8)
items.description: Switches resolution to Google Public DNS for the current session.
items.usage_tip: Handy when Cloudflare is filtered by the upstream provider.

items.title: Quad9 DNS (9.9.9.9)
items.description: Switches resolution to Quad9 and keeps the previous DNS in a backup file.
items.usage_tip: A malware-filtering alternative if the first two providers fail.

items.title: Restore Original DNS
items.description: Restores the backed-up resolv.conf and removes the temporary WAN DNS entry.
items.usage_tip: This option appears only when a backup exists; otherwise 4 means Skip.

items.title: Skip
items.description: Leaves DNS completely untouched and exits the recovery prompt.
items.usage_tip: Choose it when only HTTPS looks broken and DNS works fine.
